Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Independent checkpoints and scope proofs over the audit journal.
2	
3	This module adds two capabilities the read-only :mod:`carbon_market.audit`
4	journal does not provide on its own: an independent checkpoint file that
5	is not the journal and an offline-savable proof of a particular search.
6	
7	:func:`export` reads the complete journal snapshot under the *same*
8	``cursor`` / ``limit`` / ``op`` / ``stage`` / ``key`` arguments
9	:func:`carbon_market.audit.search` takes and returns a proof object that
10	encapsulates the query, the result page and the journal's raw bytes,
11	together with the named generation and its closed state. Each successful
12	non-duplicate export appends one anchor to the checkpoint at
13	``checkpoint_path``: the anchor binds
14	
15	* the complete event manifest -- every audit key paired with its event
16	  digest, in journal order;
17	* the SHA-256 of the journal's raw bytes (the *log digest*), so a log
18	  rotation that preserves the sealed events still produces a new anchor
19	  while the chain continues;
20	* the root head the journal declares;
21	* the digest of the previous anchor (null for the very first anchor of
22	  the checkpoint, so the stream stays one continuous chain across
23	  generations) and the closed flag.
24	
25	The query parameters and the returned page are not anchored: the proof
26	carries them and :func:`verify` recomputes the page from the embedded
27	journal bytes and parameters, so any tampering with log bytes,
28	parameters, page or cursor shows up as a mismatch. Exports of different
29	queries against an unchanged snapshot append no anchor; their proofs
30	name the snapshot's existing anchor.
31	
32	The anchor digest is the SHA-256 of that five-part binding serialized with the
33	journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention, so rotating the journal bytes
34	while the sealed chain survives keeps the anchor chain continuous --
35	every anchor also commits to the previous anchor digest.
36	
37	Generations are non-empty, unique, non-regressing names (strictly
38	ascending in code-point order): a checkpoint is an ordered list of
39	generations, and a new generation can only be created once the previous
40	one is closed. Within one generation every export must
41	preserve the already anchored events key by key and digest by digest; a
42	snapshot may keep the same manifest (a re-query, or a byte-preserving
43	log rotation) or add new keys -- which may land anywhere in code-point
44	order, since the anchored pairs are compared key by key, not by
45	position -- but a deletion, a rewrite of a known event or a retreat
46	raises ``ValueError`` and appends nothing. An export
47	identical in manifest, log digest, head and closed state is a duplicate:
48	it appends no anchor and returns a proof naming that same anchor, no
49	matter which query it carried. Passing ``final=True`` closes the current
50	generation -- the closing anchor may pin the same snapshot, only its
51	closed flag flips -- and once closed only the identical idempotent
52	export (``final=True``) is accepted.
53	
54	:func:`verify` takes *only* the checkpoint path and a previously
55	exported proof -- the journal itself is never opened -- rechecks the
56	proof envelope, recomputes the page from the embedded log bytes and
57	page, reparses the embedded journal, rechecks every anchor chain, and
58	returns the proof's original search result together with its generation
59	and closed state. Any change to the embedded log bytes, parameters, page
60	content, cursor or any digest raises ``ValueError``.
61	
62	:func:`verify_bundle` is the offline entry for a downloaded pair: it
63	takes the checkpoint file, the saved proof file and the strong entity
64	tag the download carried, recomputes the tag from the checkpoint's raw
65	bytes before anything else, and then applies the same checkpoint and
66	proof validation as :func:`verify` against the single locked snapshot
67	it read, so a racing same-directory replacement can only yield a
68	self-consistent old or new combination. Structural failures (encoding,
69	JSON grammar, field shapes) raise plain ``ValueError`` while every
70	tag, digest-chain, generation, anchor, closed-state or page mismatch
71	raises ``_MismatchError``, a ``ValueError`` subclass that lets the
72	command-line entry tell a malformed bundle apart from a failed
73	verification.
74	
75	Exports only accept a complete version 2 journal: a version 1 journal,
76	a broken digest chain or a malformed checkpoint structure raises
77	``ValueError``. Invalid argument types, an empty generation name, a
78	non-boolean ``final`` or out-of-range search parameters are rejected
79	with ``ValueError`` *before any file is read*. A missing audit journal,
80	a checkpoint required for verification, or a missing checkpoint parent
81	directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; every other locking or I/O
82	failure surfaces unchanged as ``OSError``.
83	
84	An export holds the journal's shared kernel flock and the checkpoint's
85	exclusive kernel flock together, and the checkpoint commits via a
86	same-directory temporary file that is written and fsynced, moved over
87	the checkpoint with :func:`os.replace` and followed by a directory
88	fsync. A commit failure therefore never leaves a new anchor behind nor
89	returns a proof; concurrent appenders serialize and each observes
90	either the complete previous checkpoint or the complete new one, and a
91	restarted process continues the same anchor chain from the persisted
92	checkpoint.
93	"""
94	
95	from __future__ import annotations
96	
97	import contextlib
98	import fcntl
99	import hashlib
100	import json
101	import os
102	import re
103	import tempfile
104	import threading
105	from typing import Any, Iterator
106	
107	from . import audit
108	from ._jsonio import finite_loads, strict_loads
109	
110	__all__ = ["export", "verify", "verify_bundle", "read_snapshot"]
111	
112	_VERSION = 1
113	_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "generations")
114	_GENERATION_FIELDS = ("name", "anchors")
115	_ANCHOR_FIELDS = ("manifest", "log_digest", "head", "previous", "closed",
116	                  "digest")
117	_PROOF_FIELDS = ("version", "generation", "params", "result", "log_bytes",
118	                 "log_digest", "head", "closed", "anchor_digest")
119	_PARAM_FIELDS = ("cursor", "limit", "op", "stage", "key")
120	_HEXADECIMAL = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")
121	# A downloaded checkpoint is identified by exactly one strong entity
122	# tag: one double-quoted string of 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the
123	# SHA-256 of the complete checkpoint bytes -- the same shape the
124	# conditional download accepts and serves.
125	_ETAG_RE = re.compile(r'"[0-9a-f]{64}"')
126	
127	
128	class _MismatchError(ValueError):
129	    """A digest-chain or cross-reference mismatch, not a format error.
130	
131	    Both downloaded files failing their *structural* checks (encoding,
132	    JSON grammar, field shapes) raise plain ``ValueError`` like before;
133	    a tag, digest chain, generation, anchor, closed-state or page
134	    mismatch raises this subclass instead, so the offline bundle
135	    verifier can tell a malformed bundle apart from a well-formed one
136	    that does not check out. Every existing caller still sees a
137	    ``ValueError``.
138	    """
139	
140	
141	class _CheckpointStore:
142	    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
143	        self.realpath = realpath
144	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
145	
146	
147	_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
148	_stores: dict[str, _CheckpointStore] = {}
149	
150	
151	def _get_store(realpath: str) -> _CheckpointStore:
152	    with _stores_lock:
153	        store = _stores.get(realpath)
154	        if store is None:
155	            store = _CheckpointStore(realpath)
156	            _stores[realpath] = store
157	        return store
158	
159	
160	@contextlib.contextmanager
161	def _file_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
162	    # Same flock discipline as the journal: the companion lock file is
163	    # never unlinked and the kernel releases the flock on process exit.
164	    lock_path = realpath + ".lock"
165	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
166	    try:
167	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
168	        try:
169	            yield
170	        finally:
171	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
172	    finally:
173	        os.close(fd)
174	
175	
176	def _is_digest(value: object) -> bool:
177	    return isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 64 \
178	        and all(char in _HEXADECIMAL for char in value)
179	
180	
181	def _compact(payload: Any) -> bytes:
182	    # The journal's compact UTF-8 JSON convention: compact separators,
183	    # non-ASCII written through. Used for every digest here.
184	    return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
185	                      allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8")
186	
187	
188	def _anchor_digest(manifest: list[list[Any]], log_digest: str,
189	                   head: str | None, previous: str | None,
190	                   closed: bool) -> str:
191	    return hashlib.sha256(_compact(
192	        [manifest, log_digest, head, previous, closed])).hexdigest()
193	
194	
195	def _check_params(cursor: object, limit: object, op: object, stage: object,
196	                  key: object) -> None:
197	    # Mirror audit.search exactly; the validation happens before any file
198	    # is touched, so an out-of-range parameter never reads the journal.
199	    if cursor is not None and (not isinstance(cursor, str) or not cursor):
200	        raise ValueError("cursor must be None or a non-empty string")
201	    if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) \
202	            or not 1 <= limit <= audit._MAX_LIMIT:
203	        raise ValueError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
204	    if op is not None and op not in audit._OPS:
205	        raise ValueError('op filter must be "copy" or "restore"')
206	    if stage is not None and stage not in audit._SEARCH_STAGES:
207	        raise ValueError(
208	            "stage filter must be one of 成功, 校验, 执行, 同步, 回滚")
209	    if key is not None and (not isinstance(key, str) or not key):
210	        raise ValueError("key filter must be a non-empty string")
211	
212	
213	def _params_dict(cursor: str | None, limit: int, op: str | None,
214	                 stage: str | None, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
215	    return {"cursor": cursor, "limit": limit, "op": op, "stage": stage,
216	            "key": key}
217	
218	
219	def _manifest(document: dict[str, Any]) -> list[list[Any]]:
220	    # The complete snapshot inventory: every audit key in journal order
221	    # paired with the exact digest its sealed chain gives it. Comparing
222	    # manifests item by item enforces "known events unchanged, only new
223	    # keys added" without trusting the journal bytes alone.
224	    chain = document["chain"]
225	    return [[audit_key, chain[audit_key][1]]
226	            for audit_key in document["events"]]
227	
228	
229	def _validate_manifest(raw: object) -> list[list[Any]]:
230	    if not isinstance(raw, list):
231	        raise ValueError("anchor manifest must be a list of "
232	                         "[audit key, event digest] pairs")
233	    manifest: list[list[Any]] = []
234	    last_key: str | None = None
235	    for item in raw:
236	        if not isinstance(item, list) or len(item) != 2 \
237	                or not isinstance(item[0], str) or not item[0] \
238	                or not _is_digest(item[1]):
239	            raise ValueError("anchor manifest entries must be "
240	                             "[non-empty key, 64-digit hex digest]")
241	        if last_key is not None and item[0] <= last_key:
242	            raise ValueError("anchor manifest must be ordered by key "
243	                             "code point without repeats")
244	        manifest.append([item[0], item[1]])
245	        last_key = item[0]
246	    return manifest
247	
248	
249	def _check_extension(old_manifest: list[list[Any]],
250	                     new_manifest: list[list[Any]]) -> None:
251	    # The old snapshot must survive key by key: every anchored key keeps
252	    # its exact digest, while new keys may land anywhere in code-point
253	    # order -- the manifests are compared as key/digest pairs, not by
254	    # position. Fewer entries (retreat), a missing old key (deletion) or
255	    # a changed digest under a known key (rewrite) all surface here.
256	    # Equal manifests (re-query or byte-level log rotation with same
257	    # events) are permitted by the caller and never reach this check.
258	    if len(new_manifest) <= len(old_manifest):
259	        raise _MismatchError("a generation only accepts snapshots that add "
260	                             "new audit events")
261	    new_digests = {audit_key: digest for audit_key, digest in new_manifest}
262	    for audit_key, digest in old_manifest:
263	        if new_digests.get(audit_key) != digest:
264	            raise _MismatchError("a generation cannot rewrite, delete or "
265	                                 "reorder an already anchored event")
266	
267	
268	def _validate_checkpoint(data: object) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
269	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_ROOT_FIELDS):
270	        raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be an object with keys "
271	                         "version and generations, in that order")
272	    version = data["version"]
273	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool) \
274	            or version != _VERSION:
275	        raise ValueError("unsupported checkpoint version")
276	    generations_raw = data["generations"]
277	    if not isinstance(generations_raw, list):
278	        raise ValueError("checkpoint generations must be a list")
279	    if not generations_raw:
280	        # export only creates a checkpoint together with its first
281	        # generation, so a persisted empty list is structural damage.
282	        raise ValueError("checkpoint must carry at least one generation")
283	
284	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
285	    generations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
286	    # The previous-anchor chain runs across the whole checkpoint: the
287	    # first anchor of a later generation names the last anchor of the
288	    # closed previous generation, so the stream never forks.
289	    previous: str | None = None
290	    for gen_position, generation_raw in enumerate(generations_raw):
291	        is_last_generation = gen_position == len(generations_raw) - 1
292	        if not isinstance(generation_raw, dict) \
293	                or list(generation_raw.keys()) != list(_GENERATION_FIELDS):
294	            raise ValueError("each generation must be an object with keys "
295	                             "name and anchors, in that order")
296	        name = generation_raw["name"]
297	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
298	            raise ValueError("generation name must be a non-empty string")
299	        if name in seen_names:
300	            raise ValueError("generation names must not repeat")
301	        if generations and name <= generations[-1]["name"]:
302	            # Names open in strictly ascending code-point order; an
303	            # equal-or-earlier name is a repeat or a regression.
304	            raise ValueError("generation names must not regress")
305	        seen_names.add(name)
306	        anchors_raw = generation_raw["anchors"]
307	        if not isinstance(anchors_raw, list) or not anchors_raw:
308	            raise ValueError("each generation must carry at least one anchor")
309	
310	        anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
311	        for index, anchor_raw in enumerate(anchors_raw):
312	            is_last_anchor = index == len(anchors_raw) - 1
313	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw, dict) \
314	                    or list(anchor_raw.keys()) != list(_ANCHOR_FIELDS):
315	                raise ValueError("each anchor must be an object with keys "
316	                                 "manifest, log_digest, head, previous, "
317	                                 "closed and digest, in that order")
318	            manifest = _validate_manifest(anchor_raw["manifest"])
319	            if not _is_digest(anchor_raw["log_digest"]):
320	                raise ValueError("anchor log_digest must be a 64-digit "
321	                                 "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
322	            head = anchor_raw["head"]
323	            if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
324	                raise ValueError("anchor head must be null or a 64-digit "
325	                                 "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
326	            declared_previous = anchor_raw["previous"]
327	            if index > 0 and not _is_digest(declared_previous):
328	                raise ValueError("anchor previous digest must be a "
329	                                 "64-digit hexadecimal digest")
330	            if declared_previous != previous:
331	                raise _MismatchError("anchor previous digest does not "
332	                                     "continue the chain")
333	            if not isinstance(anchor_raw["closed"], bool):
334	                raise ValueError("anchor closed must be a boolean")
335	            digest = anchor_raw["digest"]
336	            if not _is_digest(digest):
337	                raise ValueError("anchor digest must be a 64-digit "
338	                                 "lowercase hexadecimal digest")
339	            expected = _anchor_digest(manifest, anchor_raw["log_digest"],
340	                                      head, previous, anchor_raw["closed"])
341	            if digest != expected:
342	                raise _MismatchError("anchor digest does not match its "
343	                                     "content")
344	
345	            if anchors:
346	                earlier = anchors[-1]
347	                if earlier["closed"]:
348	                    raise _MismatchError("a closed anchor cannot be followed "
349	                                         "inside its generation")
350	                # Consecutive anchors either pin the same manifest (a
351	                # byte-level log rotation with the events intact, or the
352	                # closing anchor flipping the closed flag) or extend it
353	                # with new keys anywhere in code-point order while every
354	                # anchored pair survives; anything else is a rewrite.
355	                if manifest == earlier["manifest"]:
356	                    if head != earlier["head"]:
357	                        raise _MismatchError("a same-snapshot anchor cannot "
358	                                             "move the root digest")
359	                    if anchor_raw["log_digest"] == earlier["log_digest"] \
360	                            and anchor_raw["closed"] == earlier["closed"]:
361	                        raise _MismatchError("a duplicate anchor changes "
362	                                             "nothing")
363	                else:
364	                    _check_extension(earlier["manifest"], manifest)
365	            if anchor_raw["closed"] and not is_last_anchor:
366	                raise _MismatchError("only the last anchor of a generation "
367	                                     "may be closed")
368	
369	            anchor = {"manifest": manifest,
370	                      "log_digest": anchor_raw["log_digest"], "head": head,
371	                      "previous": declared_previous,
372	                      "closed": anchor_raw["closed"], "digest": digest}
373	            anchors.append(anchor)
374	            previous = digest
375	
376	        if not is_last_generation and not anchors[-1]["closed"]:
377	            # An open generation may only be the last one of the
378	            # checkpoint: any following generation proves it was closed.
379	            raise _MismatchError("a new generation can only start after "
380	                                 "the previous one is closed")
381	        generations.append({"name": name, "anchors": anchors})
382	    return generations

386	                                             bytes | None]:

388	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
389	            raw = handle.read()

391	        return None, None

394	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
395	        raise ValueError(
396	            f"checkpoint file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
397	    try:

399	    except ValueError as exc:

401	            f"checkpoint file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
402	    return _validate_checkpoint(data), raw

419	def _commit_checkpoint(realpath: str, directory: str, payload: bytes,
420	                       old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
421	    # Same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace, directory fsync --
422	    # with a rollback if anything fails after the replace, so a failed
423	    # commit never leaves the new anchor behind. The pre-call bytes are
424	    # staged back over the file (or the file removed when it did not
425	    # exist) and the directory synced again, all while the exclusive
426	    # lock is held; a failed rollback surfaces chained after the first
427	    # error.
428	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
429	        dir=directory, prefix=".audit-proof-", suffix=".tmp")
430	    try:
431	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
432	            handle.write(payload)
433	            handle.flush()
434	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
435	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
436	    except BaseException as first:
437	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
438	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
439	        raise
440	    try:
441	        _fsync_dir(directory)
442	    except BaseException as first:
443	        audit._rollback(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
444	        raise

477	def export(
478	    audit_path: str,
479	    checkpoint_path: str,
480	    generation: str,
481	    final: bool = False,
482	    cursor: str | None = None,
483	    limit: int = audit._DEFAULT_LIMIT,
484	    op: str | None = None,
485	    stage: str | None = None,
486	    key: str | None = None,
487	) -> dict[str, Any]:
488	    """Export a verifiable proof and anchor it in the checkpoint.
489	
490	    ``audit_path`` and ``checkpoint_path`` must be non-empty strings;
491	    ``generation`` must be a non-empty string and ``final`` a boolean.
492	    The search arguments follow :func:`carbon_market.audit.search`. All
493	    argument errors raise ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
494	
495	    A missing audit journal raises ``FileNotFoundError``; so does a
496	    missing parent directory of a checkpoint that must be created. A
497	    version 1 journal, an incomplete digest chain, a malformed
498	    checkpoint, a repeated generation name or an export that reopens a
499	    past generation, an attempt to open a new generation while the
500	    previous one is still open, an export that deletes or rewrites
501	    events of the current generation, or any non-identical export of a
502	    closed generation raises ``ValueError``. Remaining locking or I/O
503	    failures raise ``OSError``.
504	
505	    Returns the offline proof dict. A repeat of an export whose content
506	    and closed state are identical appends nothing and returns a proof
507	    naming the same anchor. With ``final=True`` the appended anchor closes
508	    generation -- it may pin the same snapshot -- after which only the
509	    identical idempotent export (``final=True``) is accepted.
510	    """
511	    for value in (audit_path, checkpoint_path):
512	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
513	            raise ValueError("audit_path and checkpoint_path must be "
514	                             "non-empty strings")
515	    if not isinstance(generation, str) or not generation:
516	        raise ValueError("generation must be a non-empty string")
517	    if not isinstance(final, bool):
518	        raise ValueError("final must be a boolean")
519	    _check_params(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
520	
521	    audit_real = os.path.realpath(audit_path)
522	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
523	    checkpoint_store = _get_store(checkpoint_real)
524	    with checkpoint_store.lock:
525	        # Hold the journal's shared lock and the checkpoint's exclusive
526	        # lock together until the commit lands, so audit.record cannot
527	        # rotate the journal while its bytes are sealed into an anchor.
528	        with audit._file_lock(audit_real, shared=True):
529	            # Read inside the shared flock exactly like the read-only
530	            # audit queries: a racing audit.record is observed as one
531	            # complete document or the other, never a half-replaced
532	            # file. A missing journal surfaces as FileNotFoundError.
533	            with open(audit_real, "rb") as handle:
534	                raw = handle.read()
535	            document = _parse_journal_snapshot(audit_real, raw)
536	            with _file_lock(checkpoint_real):
537	                generations, old_bytes = _read_checkpoint(checkpoint_real)
538	                if generations is None:
539	                    generations = []
540	
541	                params = _params_dict(cursor, limit, op, stage, key)
542	                # Compute the page from the exact bytes in hand; this is
543	                # the same filter/pagination audit.search applies.
544	                result = _search_document(document, params)
545	                manifest = _manifest(document)
546	                head = document["head"]
547	                log_digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
548	                names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
549	
550	                def identical(item: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
551	                    return (item["manifest"] == manifest
552	                            and item["log_digest"] == log_digest
553	                            and item["head"] == head)
554	
555	                if generation in names:
556	                    position = names.index(generation)
557	                    if position != len(generations) - 1:
558	                        # A past generation can never be reopened.
559	                        raise ValueError("a past generation cannot be "
560	                                         "exported again")
561	                    current = generations[position]
562	                    anchors = current["anchors"]
563	                    last = anchors[-1]
564	
565	                    if last["closed"]:
566	                        # Once closed the only accepted export is the
567	                        # idempotent one: final stays true and the
568	                        # snapshot is byte-for-byte the same -- events,
569	                        # log bytes and root head. The query may differ,
570	                        # since verify recomputes the page from the
571	                        # embedded log and parameters.
572	                        if not final or not identical(last):
573	                            raise ValueError("a closed generation only "
574	                                             "accepts the identical "
575	                                             "idempotent export")
576	                        return _build_proof(
577	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
578	                            head, True, last["digest"])
579	
580	                    # Still open. Same events, same bytes, same head and
581	                    # not closing: the duplicate export appends nothing
582	                    # and returns the proof of the latest anchor. The
583	                    # manifest must equal the latest anchor's, so an
584	                    # older snapshot cannot mask a retreat.
585	                    if not final and manifest == last["manifest"] \
586	                            and identical(last):
587	                        return _build_proof(
588	                            generation, params, result, raw, log_digest,
589	                            head, False, last["digest"])
590	
591	                    # Otherwise append: the manifest grows (strict
592	                    # extension), stays identical with rotated log
593	                    # bytes, or stays identical while final flips the
594	                    # closed flag. A smaller or rewritten manifest is
595	                    # rejected.
596	                    if manifest != last["manifest"]:
597	                        _check_extension(last["manifest"], manifest)
598	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
599	                                              last["digest"], final)
600	                    anchors.append(new_anchor)
601	                else:
602	                    if generations and not \
603	                            generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["closed"]:
604	                        raise ValueError("a new generation can only be "
605	                                         "started after the previous one "
606	                                         "is closed")
607	                    if generations and generation <= generations[-1]["name"]:
608	                        raise ValueError("generation names must not "
609	                                         "regress")
610	                    previous_digest = (
611	                        None if not generations
612	                        else generations[-1]["anchors"][-1]["digest"])
613	                    new_anchor = _make_anchor(manifest, log_digest, head,
614	                                              previous_digest, final)
615	                    generations.append(
616	                        {"name": generation, "anchors": [new_anchor]})
617	
618	                _commit_checkpoint(
619	                    checkpoint_real,
620	                    os.path.dirname(checkpoint_real) or ".",
621	                    _serialize_checkpoint(generations), old_bytes)
622	                return _build_proof(generation, params, result, raw,
623	                                    log_digest, head, final,
624	                                    new_anchor["digest"])
625

627	def _validate_proof(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
628	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or list(data.keys()) != list(_PROOF_FIELDS):
629	        raise ValueError("proof must be an object with the exported fields "
630	                         "in their original order")
631	    if not isinstance(data["version"], int) \
632	            or isinstance(data["version"], bool) \
633	            or data["version"] != _VERSION:
634	        raise ValueError("unsupported proof version")
635	    if not isinstance(data["generation"], str) or not data["generation"]:
636	        raise ValueError("proof generation must be a non-empty string")
637	    params = data["params"]
638	    if not isinstance(params, dict) \
639	            or list(params.keys()) != list(_PARAM_FIELDS):
640	        raise ValueError("proof params must be the exported query "
641	                         "parameters")
642	    _check_params(params["cursor"], params["limit"], params["op"],
643	                  params["stage"], params["key"])
644	    result = data["result"]
645	    if not isinstance(result, dict) \
646	            or list(result.keys()) != ["events", "next"]:
647	        raise ValueError("proof result must be the exported search result")
648	    if not isinstance(result["events"], list):
649	        raise ValueError("proof result events must be a list")
650	    next_cursor = result["next"]
651	    if next_cursor is not None and (not isinstance(next_cursor, str)
652	                                    or not next_cursor):
653	        raise ValueError("proof result next must be null or a non-empty "
654	                         "string")
655	    if not isinstance(data["log_bytes"], str):
656	        raise ValueError("proof log_bytes must be a string")
657	    if not _is_digest(data["log_digest"]):
658	        raise ValueError("proof log_digest must be a 64-digit lowercase "
659	                         "hexadecimal digest")
660	    head = data["head"]
661	    if head is not None and not _is_digest(head):
662	        raise ValueError("proof head must be null or a 64-digit lowercase "
663	                         "hexadecimal digest")
664	    if not isinstance(data["closed"], bool):
665	        raise ValueError("proof closed must be a boolean")
666	    if not _is_digest(data["anchor_digest"]):
667	        raise ValueError("proof anchor_digest must be a 64-digit lowercase "
668	                         "hexadecimal digest")
669	    return data

672	def _search_document(document: dict[str, Any], params: dict[str, Any]) \
673	        -> dict[str, Any]:
674	    # Recompute audit.search's result from an in-memory document so
675	    # verify never needs the journal file itself.
676	    cursor = params["cursor"]
677	    limit = params["limit"]
678	    matches: list[list[Any]] = []
679	    for audit_key, event in document["events"].items():
680	        if cursor is not None and audit_key <= cursor:
681	            continue
682	        if not audit._matches(event, params["op"], params["stage"],
683	                              params["key"]):
684	            continue
685	        matches.append([audit_key, dict(event)])
686	        if len(matches) > limit:
687	            break
688	    if len(matches) > limit:
689	        page = matches[:limit]
690	        return {"events": page, "next": page[-1][0]}
691	    return {"events": matches, "next": None}

694	def _verify_proof(generations: list[dict[str, Any]],
695	                  clean: dict[str, Any],
696	                  checkpoint_real: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
697	    # The cross-checks every verified proof must pass against one
698	    # checkpoint snapshot: the named generation and anchor must be
699	    # recorded, the embedded log bytes must hash to the anchored log
700	    # digest and reparse as a sealed version 2 journal whose manifest
701	    # and root head the anchor pins, and the page must recompute from
702	    # the embedded log and parameters. Every failure here is a
703	    # mismatch, never a format error.
704	    names = [item["name"] for item in generations]
705	    if clean["generation"] not in names:
706	        raise _MismatchError("proof generation is not recorded in the "
707	                             "checkpoint")
708	    generation = generations[names.index(clean["generation"])]
709	    anchor = next((item for item in generation["anchors"]
710	                   if item["digest"] == clean["anchor_digest"]), None)
711	    if anchor is None:
712	        raise _MismatchError("proof anchor is not recorded in the "
713	                             "checkpoint")
714	
715	    params = clean["params"]
716	    raw = clean["log_bytes"].encode("utf-8")
717	    if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != clean["log_digest"]:
718	        raise _MismatchError("proof log bytes do not match their log "
719	                             "digest")
720	    if clean["log_digest"] != anchor["log_digest"]:
721	        raise _MismatchError("proof log digest is not bound to the anchor")
722	    try:
723	        document = audit._parse_document(checkpoint_real, raw)
724	        audit._ensure_chain(document)
725	    except ValueError as exc:
726	        raise _MismatchError(str(exc)) from exc
727	    if document["version"] != 2:
728	        raise _MismatchError("proof requires a sealed version 2 audit "
729	                             "journal")
730	    if clean["head"] != document["head"] \
731	            or anchor["head"] != document["head"]:
732	        raise _MismatchError("proof root digest does not match the "
733	                             "journal")
734	    if _manifest(document) != anchor["manifest"]:
735	        raise _MismatchError("proof event manifest does not match the "
736	                             "anchor")
737	    if clean["closed"] != anchor["closed"]:
738	        raise _MismatchError("proof closed state does not match the "
739	                             "anchor")
740	
741	    recomputed = _search_document(document, params)
742	    if recomputed != clean["result"]:
743	        raise _MismatchError("proof result does not follow from the "
744	                             "embedded log and parameters")
745	    return {"events": clean["result"]["events"],
746	            "next": clean["result"]["next"],
747	            "generation": clean["generation"],
748	            "closed": anchor["closed"]}
749

751	def verify(checkpoint_path: str, proof: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
752	    """Verify an exported proof solely against the checkpoint.
753	
754	    The journal is not opened: the proof carries the journal's raw
755	    bytes, parameters and result. ``checkpoint_path`` must be a
756	    non-empty string and ``proof`` an object previously returned by
757	    :func:`export`.
758	
759	    The embedded log bytes must hash to the proof's log digest, parse as
760	    a complete version 2 journal whose event manifest and root head
761	    match the anchor the proof names in the named generation of the
762	    checkpoint, and the page must recompute from the embedded log and
763	    parameters. Every anchor chain in the checkpoint is rechecked as
764	    well. Success returns
765	    ``{"events": ..., "next": ..., "generation": ..., "closed": ...}``
766	    -- the original search result together with its generation and
767	    closed state.
768	
769	    A missing checkpoint raises ``FileNotFoundError``; any proof or
770	    checkpoint mismatch -- including changed log bytes, parameters,
771	    page content, cursor or any digest -- raises ``ValueError``; other
772	    I/O failures raise ``OSError``.
773	    """
774	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_path, str) or not checkpoint_path:
775	        raise ValueError("checkpoint_path must be a non-empty string")
776	
777	    clean = _validate_proof(proof)
778	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
779	    with _file_lock(checkpoint_real, shared=True):
780	        generations, _ = _read_checkpoint(checkpoint_real)
781	    if generations is None:
782	        raise FileNotFoundError(
783	            f"checkpoint file {checkpoint_real!r} does not exist")
784	    return _verify_proof(generations, clean, checkpoint_real)

789	    # negative-zero or non-finite number literal, or a JSON grammar
790	    # error is a format error of the bundle, never a mismatch.

794	        raise ValueError("bundle file is not valid UTF-8") from exc
795	    try:

801	def verify_bundle(checkpoint_path: str, proof_path: str,
802	                  etag: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
803	    """Verify a downloaded checkpoint/proof pair entirely offline.
804	
805	    ``checkpoint_path`` and ``proof_path`` must be non-empty strings and
806	    ``etag`` a single strong entity tag -- one double-quoted string of
807	    64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, exactly as the checkpoint
808	    download's ``ETag`` header carried it. Argument errors raise
809	    ``ValueError`` before any file is read.
810	
811	    The checkpoint is opened, read, hashed, parsed and structurally
812	    validated under the *same* shared kernel flock an export or a
813	    download serializes against, and the whole verification runs on
814	    that one snapshot: a same-directory atomic replacement racing the
815	    read is observed as either the complete old combination or the
816	    complete new one, never a mix of two versions. The tag is
817	    recomputed from the raw checkpoint bytes first and a mismatch fails
818	    immediately, before any further parsing. The proof file is then
819	    read under the same lock and both files are checked as UTF-8 JSON
820	    (negative-zero and non-finite number literals are format errors),
821	    the checkpoint passes the complete anchor-chain validation, and the
822	    proof passes the same offline checks :func:`verify` applies --
823	    embedded log bytes, query parameters, recomputed page, cursor and
824	    root digest, with the generation, anchor and closed state taken
825	    from the checkpoint snapshot in hand. Nothing is rewritten.
826	
827	    Returns the same result dict as :func:`verify`. A missing file
828	    raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an encoding, JSON or structural error
829	    in either file raises ``ValueError``; a tag, digest-chain,
830	    generation, anchor, closed-state or page mismatch raises
831	    ``_MismatchError`` (also a ``ValueError``); every other locking or
832	    I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
833	    """
834	    for value in (checkpoint_path, proof_path):
835	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
836	            raise ValueError("checkpoint_path and proof_path must be "
837	                             "non-empty strings")
838	    if not isinstance(etag, str) or not _ETAG_RE.fullmatch(etag):
839	        raise ValueError("etag must be a single strong tag: a quoted "
840	                         "64-digit lowercase hexadecimal digest")
841	
842	    checkpoint_real = os.path.realpath(checkpoint_path)
